title: Discover Colorado: Geography, Culture, and History
description: Explore the Centennial State with our evergreen guide to Colorado's geography, rich history, culture, and iconic natural landmarks.

sections.heading: Introduction to the Centennial State
paragraphs: Colorado, often known as the Centennial State due to its admission to the Union 100 years after the signing of the Declaration of Independence, is a destination defined by its dramatic landscapes. Located in the Mountain West subregion of the United States, it is famous for its vivid topography, which encompasses vast plains, arid deserts, deep canyons, and towering mountain ranges.

The state capital and most populous city is Denver, which sits exactly one mile above sea level, earning it the famous moniker 'The Mile High City.' Colorado attracts millions of visitors and new residents every year who are drawn to its natural beauty, thriving cultural scene, and reputation for an active, outdoor-oriented lifestyle.

sections.heading: The Majesty of the Rocky Mountains
paragraphs: The defining geographic feature of Colorado is the Rocky Mountains, which bisect the state from north to south. The Continental Divide runs right along the crest of these mountains, determining the flow of rivers toward either the Atlantic or Pacific Oceans.

Colorado contains the highest concentration of fourteeners—mountain peaks that exceed 14,000 feet in elevation—in the United States, boasting 58 such peaks. Among them is Mount Elbert, the highest summit in the Rockies, reaching an elevation of 14,440 feet. This rugged terrain makes the state a premier global destination for mountaineering, hiking, rock climbing, and winter sports.

sections.heading: A Rich History of Native Peoples and Pioneers
paragraphs: Long before it became a territory and later a state in 1876, Colorado was home to numerous Indigenous peoples, including the Ute, Cheyenne, Arapaho, and Pueblo nations, many of whom left remarkable architectural heritage, such as the cliff dwellings at Mesa Verde.

The region experienced a massive cultural and economic shift with the Pike's Peak Gold Rush of 1859, which brought tens of thousands of prospectors to the area, encapsulated by the famous slogan 'Pike's Peak or Bust.' This influx rapidly accelerated settlement, established numerous mountain mining towns, and laid the groundwork for the modern transportation and rail networks that crisscross the state today.

sections.heading: Diverse Ecosystems and National Parks
paragraphs: Despite its reputation for snowy alpine peaks, Colorado boasts remarkable ecological diversity. The state features four national parks: Rocky Mountain National Park, Mesa Verde National Park, Great Sand Dunes National Park and Preserve, and Black Canyon of the Gunnison National Park.

From the towering sand dunes backed by snow-capped mountains in the south to the deep, steep-walled gorges carved by the Gunnison River, these protected lands showcase a wide variety of flora and fauna. Visitors can encounter wildlife ranging from elk and bighorn sheep to black bears and mountain lions across these varied habitats.

sections.heading: Culture, Cuisine, and Economy
paragraphs: Colorado's culture is a vibrant blend of traditional Western heritage and modern innovation. Cities like Boulder, Colorado Springs, and Fort Collins serve as hubs for technology, education, and the arts, while historic towns maintain their 19th-century architecture and mining-era charm.

The culinary scene heavily features local ingredients, including Rocky Mountain trout, Palisade peaches, Olathe sweet corn, and green chilis, which are a staple of the region's distinct Southwestern-influenced cuisine. Craft brewing has also flourished in the state, making it one of the leading producers of independent craft beer in the country.

faq.q: Why is Colorado called the Centennial State?
faq.a: Colorado received its nickname because it was admitted to the United States as the 38th state in 1876, exactly 100 years after the signing of the Declaration of Independence in 1776.
A fourteener is a mountain peak that rises at least 14,000 feet above sea level. Colorado is home to 58 of these majestic peaks, attracting hikers and climbers from around the world.
Denver is officially known as the 'Mile High City' because its elevation is exactly one mile, or 5,280 feet, above sea level.
